section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining the relationships between early memories of warmth and safeness with peers, self-compassion, social safeness, and body appreciation in a female emerging adult sample. The study used path analyses to test a theoretical model showing that self-compassion and social safeness mediate the relationship between early peer relationships and body appreciation, with BMI showing direct effects on body appreciation and disordered eating. The authors acknowledge limitations including the cross-sectional design, female-only sample, and reliance on self-report measures, and suggest future research should explore generalization to male samples and other age groups.
